title: The constant sheaf on an irreducible topological space has no higher cohomology
author: The Stacks Project Authors
work: Stacks Project, chapter cohomology.tex (Cohomology of Sheaves)
source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file cohomology.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
difficulty_reason: For an irreducible topological space X and any abelian group A, the lemma shows that the cohomology of the constant sheaf vanishes in positive degrees (statement lines 3461-3466). The proof computes the values of the constant sheaf: any nonempty open subset of an irreducible space is itself irreducible and hence connected, so the constant sheaf takes the value A on every nonempty open and the value zero on the empty open, which is precisely the flasqueness condition (proof lines 3469-3474). Vanishing of higher cohomology for flasque sheaves is a previous lemma, and the conclusion follows immediately (proof lines 3475-3476). The claim is H2: a one-line computation of values plus one cited vanishing result, with nothing left to the reader.
